messages:
Maria: quick sync — want to nail down the preemptability rollout and the observable signals before we ship the API change. keep it concrete.
Alex: ok. what's the intended behavior for cohorts vs microlanes again? bullet points pls.
Maria: cohorts: long-lived allocation with epoch-based preemption points. microlanes: short, preemptible fast lanes for noisy tenants. soft-preempt = temporary demotion with reconcilation after N requests. hard-preempt = eviction at epoch boundary (rare).
Sam: tradeoff: epoch length -> smaller epochs = better fairness but more kv-cache churn (higher token cost). bigger epochs = stable caches but possible tail unfairness. we need a rule-of-thumb mapping from workload skew to epoch.
Priya: from infra side: suggest epoch range 500ms..3s with default 1s. make it tunable per-deployment. also document expected delta in token cost for a noisy tenant so ops can budget.
Alex: how do we detect "noisy"? naive QPS threshold is brittle. Jen: telemetry idea: headroom metric = kv_reuse_ratio = kv_hits_prefetch / kv_prefetch_attempts. rapid drop in kv_reuse_ratio + queue_len growth => candidate for soft-preempt.
Jen: also add a short-term derivative signal: d(kv_reuse_ratio)/dt to catch fast thrash. export as tags so we can alert.
Sam: acceptable preempt flow: 1) stop enqueue to cohort, 2) move *queued* requests to microlane, 3) let inflight finish on original lane. avoid killing in-flight.
Maria: question: moving queued requests risks out-of-order serving for clients expecting FIFO. Do we have customers relying on strict ordering? Alex: some do. we should make ordering-preserving option opt-in. default behavior: best-effort ordering. document it.
Priya: about hedging: replicate-on-hedge increases GPU spend. make replicate hedging gated by an SLA-breach probability predictor. we have a light-weight predictor in admissions that can emit p_breach per-request.
Alex: formula idea for soft-preempt duration: duration_ms = clamp((avg_kv_restore_tokens * token_cost) / C, min_ms, epoch_ms/2). pick C empirically. Sam: put C default = 50 token-cost-units to start.
Jen: logging: add trace tags: routing.decision=soft-preempt|hard-preempt|none, cohort.id, preempted=true|false, replicate=true|false. Also add numeric fields as tags: kv_reuse_ratio, headroom_estimate.
Maria: good. we also need to avoid high-cardinality metrics. for queue_len per-cohort, keep percentiles + top-100 tenants sampled. use streaming top-k sketch.
Sam: on-canary: propose rolling canary by cohort hash at 5% initially (hash % 100 < 5). monitor p50/p95/p99 and token-cost-per-request. run 48h.
Priya: infra can set an automated abort: if p99 increases > 20% OR cost delta > 30% on the canary group, rollout pause. implement as experiment guardrail.
Alex: API boundary: add optional tenant flag "preemptibility": [preemptible, non_preemptible]. default preemptible. non_preemptible should be limited to enterprise plans and require legal signoff.
Maria: error handling: if a non_preemptible tenant would be preempted by policy, return routing.error = PREEMPTION_FORBIDDEN and a short explanation in response headers.
Jen: tests: unit for admission sim, e2e load test where we inject a synthetic hot-tenant with 20x baseline QPS and assert cohort headroom drops and system routes as expected.
Sam: simulator changes: add synthetic kv_warm_cost model and sampling of request length. i can add to admission-sim repo and share results.
Priya: deploy note: infra-bot please tag the staging image and schedule canary window.
infra-bot: rollout staged: batcher-preemptability v1.4 -> staging at 2026-03-19T07:30Z. canary rule: cohort_hash mod 100 < 5.
Alex: timeline check: Maria updates RFC today, Sam posts sim results Wed, Jen dashboard mock Wed noon, Priya schedules canary Thurs.
Maria: thanks. after canary, we run a 50% expansion if stable, then GA. i'll update RFC with a state machine diagram and sample log lines.
Jen: small follow-up: include a dashboard row for replicate_cost_est and a breakdown of token cost vs latency benefit. helps justify hedging expense.
Maria: agreed. meeting adjourned — i'll ping for review when RFC updated. thanks :raised_hands:
